claims.claim: Fire and Blood doubles as a diegetic chronicle written by Maester Gyldayn whose in-world publication year is unclear.
claims.page: Book Culture and Narrative in Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: The book's opening sentence assigns history-keeping to the maesters of the Citadel, implying historiography confined to an ivory tower, unfunded and unnoticed by rulers.
claims.page: Book Culture and Narrative in Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: Contemporary fantasy assumes knowledge must be sought where it is hidden, and that the hidden truth may not in the end be trustworthy, so transmission itself is threatened.
claims.quote: might not, in the end, be trustworthy
claims.page: Book Culture and Narrative in Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: In-world histories such as Daeron's Conquest of Dorne are remembered for their inaccuracy ('vainglorious', 'boastful'), and propagandistic history-writing has otherwise died out in Westeros.
claims.page: Book Culture and Narrative in Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: The Kingsguard's White Book, a list of knights and deeds, echoes warrior chronicles such as Froissart's.
claims.page: Book Culture and Narrative in Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: Deep time is hostile to book knowledge, and the loss of knowledge is the greatest challenge to fantasy realms concerned with the distant past.
claims.quote: Deep time is hostile to book knowledge
claims.page: Book Culture and Narrative in Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire

claims.feature: chronicle to reminiscence to fairy tale
claims.claim: The Harrenhal tourney exists in three registers: the World of Ice and Fire chronicle, scattered eyewitness reminiscences, and Meera Reed's fairy-tale retelling, tracing how history becomes tale.
claims.source: Bartlomiej Blaszkiewicz, 'From Chronicle to Fairy Tale', in Marchen und Gesellschaft (WUW, 2024), pp. 163-175
claims.quote: scattered personal reminiscences of various eyewitness characters

claims.feature: imitated chronicle style plus modern simplification
claims.claim: The real authors of The World of Ice and Fire imitated the style of the medieval chronicle and synthesized it with modern simplistic historical representations.
claims.source: Maksim Kyrchanoff (Kirchanov), Journal of Frontier Studies 2018 no. 1
claims.quote: imitated the style of the medieval chronicle
claims.page: Historical grand narratives of the Seven kingdoms of Westeros

claims.claim: The imagined author orders events chronologically and periodizes into named ages (Dawn Age, Age of Heroes, Long Night, Doom of Valyria), linear yet imagined as torn apart.
claims.source: Maksim Kyrchanoff (Kirchanov), Journal of Frontier Studies 2018 no. 1
claims.quote: imagined his "linear time" as torn apart
claims.page: Historical grand narratives of the Seven kingdoms of Westeros

claims.claim: The imagined chronicler allows himself estimates of the world's age ranging from 40 to 500 thousand years, a hedge of enormous width stated flatly.
claims.source: Maksim Kyrchanoff (Kirchanov), Journal of Frontier Studies 2018 no. 1
claims.page: Historical grand narratives of the Seven kingdoms of Westeros

claims.claim: Gyldayn's Dance history rests on three fictional primary sources: Septon Eustace, Maester Munkun, and the Testimony of Mushroom.
claims.page: Badgering on Mushroom: Historiography and Outsiders in House of the Dragon

claims.claim: Mushroom peppers his account with debauchery and ribald humor and is by far the most amusing of the three chroniclers.
claims.page: Badgering on Mushroom: Historiography and Outsiders in House of the Dragon

claims.claim: The device mirrors real premodern sources (Procopius, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Froissart), which are later compilations, paraphrases and unreliable narrators.
claims.quote: later compilations, paraphrases, and unreliable narrators
claims.page: Badgering on Mushroom: Historiography and Outsiders in House of the Dragon

claims.claim: Showrunner Condal says the show left the Rashomon-style telling to the book and instead defined an objective truth, which Mondschein calls a category error about real history.
claims.quote: we kind of left that to the book
claims.page: Badgering on Mushroom: Historiography and Outsiders in House of the Dragon

claims.claim: The narrator openly admits where the history gets muddled between Eustace's sober account and Mushroom's sensational one and leaves the reader to decide.
claims.page: House of the Dragon Misses One of the Best Aspects of Fire & Blood
